The overwhelming dominance of white Chevrolet vehicles, including the Malibu, Cobalt, and Daewoo Damas microvan, immediately identifies this location as Uzbekistan. The wide, tree-lined avenues, overhead truss traffic light gantries, and three-story Soviet-era neoclassical apartment blocks housing ground-floor bridal shops are characteristic of central Tashkent, particularly along major arteries like Shota Rustaveli or Nukus Street. Phone numbers with Uzbek mobile prefixes (95, 97) on the roadside advertisement further confirm the capital city.

>>>{"country":"Uzbekistan","place":"Tashkent","lat":41.2858,"lng":69.2618}

The architectural style of the apartment blocks, the granite curbstones, and the black-and-yellow flexible road bollards are characteristic of northern Portugal. In the background stands a distinctive postmodern high-rise tower located near the Boavista district in central Porto. The view and elevation align with the residential streets just west of the Rotunda da Boavista, around Lordelo do Ouro and Massarelos.

>>>{"country":"Portugal","place":"Porto","lat":41.1558,"lng":-8.6392}

The red and green flag flying on the far left is the regional flag of the La Paz Department in Bolivia. In the background, steep dry hillsides covered in dense brick buildings are iconic to the canyon geography of the city of La Paz. This large, elevated paved public square with rows of flagpoles and metal railings is the Plaza Mayor de San Francisco in the heart of the city.
>>>{"country":"Bolivia","place":"La Paz","lat":-16.4962,"lng":-68.1368}

The image shows the colorful entrance to the "New China Children's Store" (新中国儿童用品商店), written in both English and Simplified Chinese. This well-known store is located on the famous Wangfujing pedestrian shopping street in Dongcheng District, Beijing. The Longines store on the left and the bank on the right confirm its exact spot along the western side of Wangfujing Street.

>>> {"country":"China","place":"Beijing","lat":39.9117,"lng":116.4111}

The urban courtyard setting features a mix of older low-rise structures, early 20th-century residential buildings with red clay tile roofs, and modern glass-facade infill typical of Balkan capitals. The European-style license plates with a left blue strip, combined with the distinctive round green insurance sticker on the lower windshield of the van, strongly point to Bulgaria. The dense architectural layering is characteristic of central Sofia.

>>>{"country":"Bulgaria","place":"Sofia","lat":42.6977,"lng":23.3219}

The image shows a grand neoclassical building with distinctive three-lamp street lights and European vehicles, characteristic of institutional architecture in Bucharest, Romania. Specifically, this is the northern side facade and parking area of the Bucharest National Opera (Opera Națională București). The architectural details, including the tall vertical windows, cornice, and side staircase, match the opera house located near Eroilor Park.

>>>{"country":"Romania","place":"Bucharest","lat":44.4361,"lng":26.0792}

The road signs, traffic lights, and street furniture are distinctly German. The recognizable skyline in the background, featuring skyscrapers like the Taunusturm, Eurotower, and the spire of the Commerzbank Tower, clearly identifies the city as Frankfurt am Main. The red sandstone bridge railings and street alignment place this exact view at the southern end of the Untermainbrücke, where Schweizer Straße meets Schaumainkai, looking north across the Main River.

>>> {"country":"Germany","place":"Frankfurt am Main","lat":50.1051,"lng":8.6758}

The distinctive sandstone tenement architecture, left-hand traffic, UK emergency vehicle markings, and Low Emission Zone signs point directly to Scotland. The prominent craggy hill visible straight down the street is Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh. Locating the Co-op Funeralcare on the corner right at the Low Emission Zone boundary places this at the northern end of Montrose Terrace, looking south from the junction with London Road and Easter Road.

>>> {"country":"United Kingdom","place":"Edinburgh","lat":55.9567,"lng":-3.1722}

This photograph was taken at a major Italian railway station, identifiable by the Trenitalia rolling stock, green ticket validators, and RFI digital departure boards. The platform numbering "1 Est" and "2 Est" along with the regional train bound for Ancona specifically point to the eastern bay platforms of Roma Termini. The distinctive travertine facade and long concrete overhang on the left belong to the station's Via Marsala wing.

>>>{"country":"Italy","place":"Rome","lat":41.8992,"lng":12.5055}

The architectural style, ornate black street lamps, and wide granite-paved pedestrian promenade are characteristic of Krakowskie Przedmieście in Warsaw, Poland. On the left is the Church of the Visitandines alongside the Cardinal Stefan Wyszyński monument, while the curved modernist building with ground-level arcades on the right is the famous "Dom Bez Kantów" at the corner of Królewska Street. Looking north down the street, the bell tower of St. Anne's Church is visible in the distance.

>>>{"country":"Poland","place":"Warsaw","lat":52.2408,"lng":21.0156}

The irregular fieldstone cobblestones, European license plates, and the red-brick German-style architecture visible in the window reflection strongly point to the historic port city of Klaipėda, Lithuania. The distinctive late-Soviet/postmodern building with concrete-and-metal arched overhangs above large glass windows is located in the Old Town area near Theatre Square.

>>>{"country":"Lithuania","place":"Klaipėda","lat":55.7068,"lng":21.1325}

The white Renault Clio features French text reading "Véhicule de courtoisie, Carrosserie Connan" along with the telephone number 05 62 31 54 57. In the French numbering plan, the 05 62 prefix belongs to the southwestern departments of Gers and Hautes-Pyrénées, with 05 62 31 specifically assigned to the area around Tarbes. The dark slate roofs, stone walling, and Pyrenees-style architecture further confirm a town in the Hautes-Pyrénées department near Tarbes.

>>> {"country":"France","place":"Tarbes, Hautes-Pyrénées","lat":43.2329,"lng":0.0781}

The concrete slab road, lush tropical vegetation, and roadside sari-sari store covered in advertisements for Mighty cigarettes—a major Filipino brand—clearly place this scene in the Philippines. The English signage ("STORE") and architectural style of the small wooden and corrugated metal shops are typical of rural areas across the archipelago, particularly in the Visayas and Mindanao regions.

>>> {"country":"Philippines","place":"Negros Occidental","lat":10.3547,"lng":123.0125}

This urban scene shows concrete H-style utility poles, tangled overhead wiring, and a mix of Kia, Toyota Vitz, and older Japanese JDM sedan models very typical of Paraguay. The white licence plates with red lettering, combined with the lush subtropical trees including a blooming pink lapacho in the background, point directly to the capital city of Asunción. The architecture with clay-tiled roofs, brick walls, and narrow asphalt streets is characteristic of central residential neighborhoods in Asunción.

>>> {"country":"Paraguay","place":"Asunción","lat":-25.2968,"lng":-57.6061}

The scene features right-hand traffic dominated by white second-hand Japanese vehicles (such as Toyota Probox and kei trucks), a hallmark of Myanmar's streets. The wide, straight concrete avenue with low white median blocks, utility poles, and presence of two-wheelers strongly points to a major thoroughfare in Mandalay rather than Yangon.

>>> {"country":"Myanmar","place":"Mandalay","lat":21.9750,"lng":96.0836}

The billboard on the right clearly reads "MADE IN JAMAICA," immediately identifying the country. The vehicle is driving on the left side of a divided highway featuring Jamaica's characteristic black-and-yellow striped median curbs. The flat coastal terrain, tropical scrub vegetation, and highway infrastructure are typical of the main arterial roads around Portmore and Kingston or along the North Coast Highway.

>>> {"country":"Jamaica","place":"Portmore","lat":17.9685,"lng":-76.8672}

The large storefront sign explicitly states "I ❤️ KL GIFTS MALAYSIA" along with the Malay descriptor "Kedai Cenderahati" (souvenir shop) and a business license number starting with "DBKL" (Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur). This specific souvenir shop is located in the bustling Bukit Bintang shopping and tourist district in central Kuala Lumpur, right along Jalan Bukit Bintang.

>>> {"country":"Malaysia","place":"Kuala Lumpur","lat":3.1466,"lng":101.7105}

The most direct clue is the large "ATOCHA" sign visible on the building in the background, paired with the iconic 19th-century wrought-iron and brick train shed on the right and Rafael Moneo's cylindrical modern station expansion on the left. This identifies the location as Madrid Puerta de Atocha railway station in Spain. The photo is taken looking southeast from the ramp on the northeastern side of the historic terminal near the Plaza del Emperador Carlos V.

>>> {"country":"Spain","place":"Madrid","lat":40.4077,"lng":-3.6911}

The cobblestone street, rough-cut granite retaining walls, and lush Atlantic Forest vegetation are classic features of the historic hilly neighborhoods of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Specifically, the ornate white wall with traditional glazed ceramic pinecone finials and high security fencing is iconic to the mansions of Santa Teresa and Cosme Velho. The grey Brazilian license plates and older European-style vans further confirm this location in Rio.

>>> {"country":"Brazil","place":"Rio de Janeiro","lat":-22.9218,"lng":-43.1856}

The vehicles, including a Fiat Egea, along with the typical red-trimmed prefabricated cabin and European-style license plates, clearly place this scene in Turkey. The reflection of palm trees in the glass facade of the commercial building ahead indicates a warm coastal or southern city, while the mix of older mid-rise concrete blocks and modern high-rise towers is characteristic of central İzmir around the Konak and Basmane districts.

>>>{"country":"Turkey","place":"İzmir","lat":38.4255,"lng":27.1428}

The red corrugated metal siding and the large photograph of horned sheep in front of rugged mountains are quintessential characteristics of Iceland. The storefront "Fotografí" is a well-known photography gallery and shop located on Skólavörðustígur in central Reykjavík.

>>> {"country":"Iceland","place":"Reykjavík","lat":64.1444,"lng":-21.9293}

This photo was taken on the famous Khao San Road in Bangkok, Thailand. The large red-and-black diamond sign clearly reads "The One" with "Khaosan" written underneath, alongside a neighbouring shop called "Biggaink Tattoo." The distinctive A-frame roof structure of The One Bangkok nightclub, combined with the Thai spirit house with yellow garlands at the entrance and street vendor stalls, confirms the exact spot in the Phra Nakhon district.

>>>{"country":"Thailand","place":"Bangkok","lat":13.7589,"lng":100.4973}

The pedestrian crossing signs with dashed lines, blue overhead lane-direction signs, and red asphalt cycle paths are characteristic of Lithuania. The combination of a modern Lidl supermarket opposite Soviet-era red-brick and white-panel apartment blocks is particularly typical of large Lithuanian residential districts such as those in Kaunas or Vilnius.

>>>{"country":"Lithuania","place":"Kaunas","lat":54.9255,"lng":23.9615}

The billboard on the right features Hungarian text ("Csökkentse vállalkozása áramdíját!") for the energy company E.ON, which supplies power to the Transdanubia region of Hungary. The distinctive yellow barracks-style building on the right, the multi-lane road, and the Mecsek hills rising in the background match the urban landscape of Pécs along main arterial Route 6 near 48-as tér.

>>> {"country":"Hungary","place":"Pécs","lat":46.0743,"lng":18.2398}

The overhead gantry with three tall rectangular variable speed limit displays and the T-shaped double-arm highway street lights are characteristic of Flemish highways in Belgium, particularly the Antwerp Ring Road (R1). The right-hand traffic, long white dashed lane markings, and dense interchange infrastructure further confirm the Antwerp area. The yellow truck on the right belongs to Luxtransport or a similar Benelux logistics firm, fitting the major port hub of Antwerp.

>>> {"country":"Belgium","place":"Antwerp","lat":51.2093,"lng":4.4445}

The presence of Sinhala script on the "People's Leasing" billboard, left-hand traffic, and the distinctive red three-wheeler confirm this is Sri Lanka. A "Durdans" sign, a Lanka IOC petrol station canopy, a mosque, and a large conical water tower are visible on the left side of this divided urban avenue. This specific combination of landmarks is located along Galle Road in the Wellawatte neighborhood of Colombo, looking south.

>>>{"country":"Sri Lanka","place":"Colombo","lat":6.8741,"lng":79.8605}

The yellow dashed cycling lane markings, overhead trolleybus wires, and distinctive transit stop design clearly place this location in Switzerland. On the left is the historic sandstone building of the Kunstmuseum Bern along Hodlerstrasse, while on the right is the modern rusted-steel facade of the Uptown/Metro building just north of Bern's main station.

>>> {"country":"Switzerland","place":"Bern","lat":46.9511,"lng":7.4435}

The modern institutional architecture featuring dark brick and curved concrete facades, combined with the European vehicle fleet and a yellow-bordered Nordic no-parking sign on the right wall, strongly points to Finland. The birch-like foliage and gravel parking lot are very typical of Finnish university campuses or municipal centers. I will place the guess in the central university city of Jyväskylä.

>>>{"country":"Finland","place":"Jyväskylä","lat":62.2385,"lng":25.7369}

The distinct grey limestone brick walls mixed with older red brick and modern functionalist white plaster architecture are characteristic of central Tallinn, Estonia. The small black and timber-clad geometric pavilion on the left is an urban installation created by students of the Estonian Academy of Arts, located in a gravel parking courtyard near the city center. The European license plates and northern temperate foliage further confirm the Baltic setting.

>>>{"country":"Estonia","place":"Tallinn","lat":59.4328,"lng":24.7458}

The distinctive dark pinkish-brown volcanic tuff stone apartment building on the left is an iconic architectural feature of Yerevan, Armenia. The tree-lined street, cobblestone walkway, low basalt stone wall bordering a sunken park area, and mix of Soviet-era and modern curved-glass buildings point directly to the central Kentron district of Yerevan, near Saryan Street and Main Avenue Park.

>>> {"country":"Armenia","place":"Yerevan","lat":40.1845,"lng":44.5082}

The Traditional Chinese signage, yellow-and-black striped utility poles, and horizontal traffic lights clearly place this location in Taiwan. The green street signs identify the intersection of Rehe 1st Street (熱河一街) and Qingdao Street (青島街). Additionally, the restaurant sign on the far left mentions the "Kaohsiung Medical University branch" (高醫店), pinpointing this exact intersection in the Sanmin District of Kaohsiung.

>>>{"country":"Taiwan","place":"Kaohsiung","lat":22.6438,"lng":120.3081}

The building on the right clearly displays the text "JUSTIZZENTRUM WIEN MITTE" and features a distinctive Vienna street sign reading "3., Markthallenbrücke". Across the street on the left is the Wien Mitte station and shopping mall complex, identifiable by the green "CAT" (City Airport Train) City Check-In signage. This places the viewer at the intersection of Marxergasse and Gigergasse/Invalidenstraße in Vienna's 3rd district (Landstraße).

>>> {"country":"Austria","place":"Vienna","lat":48.2073,"lng":16.3851}

The Greek script on the storefront ("ΕΜΠΟΡΙΑ... Σταύρος Στ. Μαρμαρινός") and the distinctive blue street number plate immediately place this in Greece, specifically central Athens. The narrow commercial alleyway filled with shoe shops, graffiti, and a yellow Euronet ATM is characteristic of the Monastiraki and Psyrri neighborhoods. The business name corresponds to a known footwear shop located at Normanou 8, right in the heart of Monastiraki.

>>> {"country":"Greece","place":"Athens","lat":37.9768,"lng":23.7249}

The Khmer script on the optics shop sign to the left immediately places this location in Cambodia. On the far right pillar, a small plaque reads "N. 13 A, ST. 278", and the left storefront mentions Street 63 in Khmer, corresponding to the numbered street grid of Phnom Penh. This intersection of Street 278 and Street 63 is located in the Boeung Keng Kang 1 (BKK1) district, where "Suzy! Time Cafe" operated.

>>> {"country":"Cambodia","place":"Phnom Penh","lat":11.5528,"lng":104.9250}

This photograph shows "Bågen" (The Arch), a prominent waterfront sculpture by Claes Hake located along the Göta älv river. On the left edge, the distinctive colonnade and architecture of the Gothenburg Opera (Göteborgsoperan) is clearly visible, placing this scene right on Packhuskajen in central Gothenburg, Sweden.

>>>{"country":"Sweden","place":"Gothenburg","lat":57.7110,"lng":11.9656}

This neoclassical grey stone building with a relief of Britannia in the pediment is the Old Custom House (Édifice de la Douane) in Old Montreal. The distinctive red directional street signs in the bottom right corner and the surrounding historic stone architecture confirm the location at Place Royale in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

>>>{"country":"Canada","place":"Montreal","lat":45.5036,"lng":-73.5544}

The large sign on the self-service car wash features distinctive Georgian script reading "თვითრეცხვა ბაბლი" (Self-wash Bubble), immediately placing this location in Georgia. The concrete block construction of the unfinished commercial building on the right and the suburban residential architecture in the background are very typical of the outskirts of major Georgian cities like Tbilisi.

>>> {"country":"Georgia","place":"Tbilisi","lat":41.7865,"lng":44.7661}

The left-hand traffic, distinctive rounded-top sound barriers, and a Japanese domestic market Toyota minivan with a short rectangular license plate clearly place this on an urban expressway in Japan. The architectural style of the mid-rise apartment buildings with external staircases and the overhead high-voltage power lines are characteristic of the dense suburban corridors surrounding major Japanese metropolitan areas like Tokyo or Osaka. Given the expressway barrier style, a location along the Shuto Expressway network in the Greater Tokyo Area is the strongest fit.

>>>{"country":"Japan","place":"Tokyo","lat":35.6762,"lng":139.6503}

The billboard on the left features text in the Malagasy language ("IANAO NO BOSS" and "1 TAONA") alongside the logo for BNI Madagascar at the bottom. A white Renault 4, an iconic and ubiquitous vehicle in Madagascar's capital, is parked on the left near a Ford dealership ("Materauto" / "Ocean Trade"). This commercial avenue with divided lanes and industrial showrooms corresponds to Route des Hydrocarbures in the Ankorondrano district of Antananarivo.

>>> {"country":"Madagascar","place":"Antananarivo","lat":-18.8842,"lng":47.5236}

The distinctive sidewalk paving of large concrete slabs bordered by cobblestone rows, combined with the suspended streetlamps and numerous bicycles, is characteristic of central Copenhagen, Denmark. On the left is the large modernist rear facade of the Magasin du Nord department store along Bremerholm, complete with the underground parking ramp structures in the middle of the street. The view looks northeast up Bremerholm toward the trees of Kongens Nytorv in the distance.

>>>{"country":"Denmark","place":"Copenhagen","lat":55.6789,"lng":12.5838}

The most decisive clue is the coat of arms engraved on the dark stone drinking fountain in the foreground, which is the official emblem of the City of Sarajevo, featuring stylized fortress walls above a bridge. The steep hillside in the background covered with red-tiled roofs and typical Balkan residential architecture further confirms the setting in the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This public fountain is located next to a parking area in the old part of the city.

>>> {"country":"Bosnia and Herzegovina","place":"Sarajevo","lat":43.8586,"lng":18.4365}

The distinctive rectangular white sign with a no-stopping symbol and a red warning strip at the bottom is standard municipal signage used in Belgrade, Serbia, to prohibit parking on green areas. The mid-century Yugoslav residential blocks with enclosed balconies and split air-conditioning units are typical of Belgrade neighborhoods like Palilula and Dorćol. In the background at the end of the street, the concrete structure of the Pančevo Bridge approach viaduct is visible, pinpointing this residential street near Poenkareova in the Palilula district.

>>>{"country":"Serbia","place":"Belgrade","lat":44.8195,"lng":20.4785}

The scene shows a shaded urban playground with prominent yellow ribbons tied to the fence, a widespread symbol in Israel since late 2023. Hebrew lettering is clearly visible on the white building across the street, possibly a synagogue or school, alongside typical Israeli license plates and municipal park lamps. The dense urban setting with high-rise buildings visible in the upper-left background points directly to the Tel Aviv metropolitan area.

>>>{"country":"Israel","place":"Tel Aviv","lat":32.0853,"lng":34.7818}

The strongest clues are the red-and-white Tunisian flag hanging on the building under construction in the background, the yellow taxi typical of Tunis, and the dark rear license plates. The wide new streets, modern streetlamps, and active mid-rise construction match the La Perle du Lac development along the Berges du Lac in Tunis.

>>> {"country":"Tunisia","place":"Tunis","lat":36.8355,"lng":10.2565}

The street sign clearly reads "Boulevard Aliou Ardo Sow," which is the official name given to a major section of the Voie de Dégagement Nord (VDN) highway in Dakar, Senegal. This is further confirmed by the French-language billboard featuring the Wolof word "Teral," the dry sandy median, and typical Senegalese urban architecture. We are driving along this main arterial road in the Mermoz-Sacré-Cœur area of Dakar.

>>>{"country":"Senegal","place":"Dakar","lat":14.7165,"lng":-17.4675}

The blue bike-share docks belong to the EnCicla system, and a sign in the upper right explicitly reads "Medellín," placing this in Medellín, Colombia. The station totem reads "SAN ANTONIO," located directly underneath the elevated concrete viaduct of the Medellín Metro. The surrounding shops, including "Compraventa Ideal," pinpoint this exact spot along Carrera 51 (Bolívar) beside the San Antonio metro station.

>>> {"country":"Colombia","place":"Medellín","lat":6.2479,"lng":-75.5697}

The tram tracks, concrete catenary poles with white-painted bases, and a Daewoo Lanos parked alongside other European-plated cars strongly point to Ukraine. In the background, high green sports netting and distinct stadium floodlight towers can be seen next to a brick wall. This matches the tram turnaround loop at the Academy of Arts near the Ukraina Stadium and training pitches in Snopkivskyi Park in Lviv.
>>> {"country":"Ukraine","place":"Lviv","lat":49.8235,"lng":24.0415}

This scene shows a manicured tropical botanical garden featuring a dense collection of diverse palm species, including young bottle palms and larger Phoenix palms with epiphyte-covered trunks. The paved curving path with sloped concrete curbing and lush lawn strongly resembles the Palmetum section of the National Botanical Garden in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

>>>{"country":"Dominican Republic","place":"Santo Domingo","lat":18.4952,"lng":-69.9548}

The image shows a cycle path with Norway's characteristic yellow dashed centerline running alongside railway tracks with Norwegian catenary masts. On the left is the distinctive blue-striped KLP building along Trelastgata in the Bjørvika neighborhood of Oslo, with the Nordenga Bridge crossing the tracks in the background. This places the view at Annette Thommessens plass, just east of Oslo Central Station, looking east-southeast.

>>>{"country":"Norway","place":"Oslo","lat":59.9087,"lng":10.7601}

The red-and-silver Toyota Crown Comfort taxi, left-hand traffic, British-style road markings, and ultra-dense residential skyscrapers immediately identify this as Hong Kong. The distinctive cylindrical blue glass tower on the left is the Bank of China Centre, and the MTR logo ahead marks Olympic Station spanning across the highway. This places the view on the West Kowloon Highway heading north just south of Olympic Station in Kowloon.

>>>{"country":"Hong Kong","place":"Kowloon","lat":22.3135,"lng":114.1608}

The image features traditional Korean palace architecture, including characteristic dark ceramic roof tiles (*giwa*), red wooden eaves with white-painted rafter ends, and a patterned stone-and-brick wall. On the right side, a green plaque displays the Hanja characters "景福" (Gyeongbok), directly identifying this as Gyeongbokgung Palace in central Seoul, South Korea.

>>> {"country":"South Korea","place":"Seoul","lat":37.5796,"lng":126.977}

This street scene is in Santiago, Chile, identifiable by the distinctive red-and-white Red Movilidad public bus, the black taxi with a yellow roof on the far right, and white Chilean license plates. We are looking south down Avenida Vicuña Mackenna from the wide median just south of Plaza Baquedano. The distinctive cream-and-white building on the left is the Parroquia de la Asunción, which sits on the eastern side of the avenue near Baron Pierre de Coubertin street.

>>>{"country":"Chile","place":"Santiago","lat":-33.4394,"lng":-70.6341}

The yellow rear license plate, herringbone brick road paving, and distinctive "Zone 30" and yield signage with red-brick cycle paths unmistakably place this scene in the Netherlands. The dark green bollards, grey utility box, and twin brick gatehouses at the park or cemetery entrance across the intersection are characteristic of Dutch urban edges in cities like Arnhem or Utrecht.

>>>{"country":"Netherlands","place":"Arnhem","lat":51.9851,"lng":5.8987}

The red-and-white reflective bumper tape on the vehicles and the unfinished brick architecture with rebar protruding from the roofs are classic indicators of Peru. Most decisively, the overhead traffic sign in the top left lists "AV. LA CULTURA", "URB. LA CAMPIÑA", and "CALLE BOLIVAR". This exact combination corresponds to the main arterial Avenue de la Cultura passing through the San Sebastián district of Cusco at its intersection with Calle Bolívar.

>>> {"country":"Peru","place":"Cusco","lat":-13.5318,"lng":-71.9333}

The black-and-white striped signposts, yellow-and-black painted curbs, and manicured rows of hedges with date palms are characteristic of the Abu Dhabi Emirate in the United Arab Emirates. Specifically, the low-mounted blue street sign on two posts in the median and the beige roadside electrical substation are iconic features of the road network in Al Ain.

>>> {"country":"United Arab Emirates","place":"Al Ain","lat":24.2075,"lng":55.7447}

The left-hand traffic, distinctive red-and-yellow reflective chevrons with a circular speed limit sticker on the rear of the box truck, and tropical vegetation including Araucaria trees point to coastal East Africa. The multi-lane divided highway with concrete jersey barriers separating main lanes from service lanes and modern dual-arm streetlamps is characteristic of major arterial roads in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, such as Julius Nyerere Road.

>>>{"country":"Tanzania","place":"Dar es Salaam","lat":-6.8422,"lng":39.2475}

The "INOWAI" real estate signage on the ground floor of the modernist office building on the left points directly to Luxembourg City, where the company's headquarters is located at 52 Route d'Esch. The yellow rear license plates visible on the cars ahead and the distinctive European road markings confirm Luxembourg. We are driving northeast along Route d'Esch with the trees of Parc de Merl lining the right side of the street.

>>>{"country":"Luxembourg","place":"Luxembourg City","lat":49.6052,"lng":6.1167}

This photo was taken at the Great Court of the University of Nairobi's main campus in Nairobi, Kenya. The distinctive mid-century modernist university building with ochre and white facades sits directly behind the famous curved "Fountain of Knowledge" monument on the right. In the background, the skyline of central Nairobi and a Shell petrol station along University Way are visible.

>>>{"country":"Kenya","place":"Nairobi","lat":-1.2801,"lng":36.8165}

This image shows a coastal parking lot and campervan area in Europe, indicated by the European-style no-entry sign, road markings, and "Sunlight" brand motorhome. The red and white plastic Jersey barriers, dark-backed signage, and oleander hedges are particularly characteristic of Italy. The flat lagoon landscape in the background with a small wooded island and distant port infrastructure strongly matches the Venetian Lagoon, specifically looking out from the Punta Sabbioni or Tronchetto parking areas near Venice.

>>>{"country":"Italy","place":"Venice","lat":45.4426,"lng":12.4235}

The distinctive black-and-white patterned cobblestone pavement (calçada portuguesa) and Pombaline architecture with azulejo tile facades immediately identify this as Lisbon, Portugal. Looking down the pedestrian street, the iconic Arco da Rua Augusta is clearly visible at the end of the avenue, placing this directly on Rua Augusta. The high building numbers (249 and 251) on the right side indicate we are near the northern end of the street, looking south from just below Rossio Square.

>>> {"country":"Portugal","place":"Lisbon","lat":38.7119,"lng":-9.1385}

The parking sign uses the word "tímar" (hours) on a Danish-style blue sign plate, which uniquely identifies the Faroe Islands. In the background, the distinctive angled floodlight towers of the Tórsvøllur national stadium in Tórshavn are clearly visible behind the Scania dealership. This places the view in the Gundadalur/Hoydalsvegur commercial and sports area of northern Tórshavn.

>>> {"country":"Faroe Islands","place":"Tórshavn","lat":62.0203,"lng":-6.7795}

The yellow rear licence plate, left-hand traffic, and the NCP (National Car Parks) sign on the multi-storey car park clearly place this in the United Kingdom. The distinctive curved glass skyscraper ahead is the Obel Tower, the tallest building in Ireland, located along the River Lagan in Belfast. The photo was taken from the M3 Lagan Bridge heading west towards the city centre, right next to the City Quays car park.

>>> {"country":"United Kingdom","place":"Belfast","lat":54.6033,"lng":-5.9195}

The prominent sign on the red-brick building on the left clearly reads "LINDNER" with "HOTEL CITY PLAZA" and "KÖLN" underneath.
